ttfx on Omarchy

Pipe any text through your terminal and watch it decrypt, burn, or rain down like The Matrix.

Short answer

To install ttfx on Omarchy, open a terminal and run omarchy pkg add ttfx. It is a 1.3 MB download (3.2 MB installed), version 0.5.0-3, licensed MIT. Terminal text effects as a single static binary — Rust port of terminaltexteffects. Free and open source.

On this page Install Open and use Requirements Uninstall Package facts Questions

Install ttfx on Omarchy

ttfx is a single static binary that applies flashy visual effects, such as matrix-style rain, decryption reveals, fireworks, and waves, to text piped into it, for example `ls -la | ttfx decrypt`. It is a Rust rewrite of the Python TerminalTextEffects project, built for speed: it starts in under a millisecond and reportedly runs over 27 times faster than the original, so it is practical to drop into everyday shell pipelines rather than just for one-off demos.

  1. Open a terminal.
  2. Run the install command:
    omarchy pkg add ttfx
  3. Check it landed. Pacman should list version 0.5.0-3:
    pacman -Qi ttfx

Open and use ttfx

ttfx has no window of its own: it is a command-line tool, library or system component. To see the commands it added to your PATH:

pacman -Ql ttfx | grep /usr/bin/

ttfx requirements and compatibility

  • A terminal that supports ANSI escape sequences

Dependencies Omarchy installs for you

  • gcc-libs
  • glibc

Pricing and license

Free and open source. License: MIT.

Frequently asked questions

How do I install ttfx on Omarchy?

Open a terminal and run omarchy pkg add ttfx. The download is 1.3 MB and it takes 3.2 MB once installed. Omarchy pulls in any dependencies automatically.

Is ttfx free?

Free and open source. The package is licensed MIT.

How do I uninstall ttfx?

Run omarchy pkg drop ttfx. It removes the package from your system.

What does ttfx depend on?

The package declares 2 dependencies: gcc-libs, glibc. Omarchy installs them for you.

Is ttfx a desktop app?

No. ttfx has no window of its own; it is a command-line tool, library or system component.

Is ttfx in the official Omarchy repo?

Yes. It is published as ttfx (version 0.5.0-3) in the official Omarchy package repository. Omacom makes it. Project site: https://github.com/omacom/ttfx. This site is unofficial and not affiliated with Omarchy or Omacom.
